subject: Unexpected overage: staging key traffic attributed to prod (invoice hold request)

From: Samira Khan <samira@fjord-analytics.com>

Cc: billing@fjord-analytics.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Unexplained spike on June 9 — asking to hold invoice

Hi Ben,

We noticed a ~480% jump in token consumption on our June 9 invoice line (attached snapshot). Our engineering team confirmed that a staging API key landed in production deploys for a ~2.5 hour window last night; that traffic should not be billable to our prod contract. Can you please: 1) pause any collection on the related invoice while we investigate, 2) provide the per-request logs/attribution slices for that window, and 3) confirm how Redwood treats cross-key attribution when requests come from the same org but different keys?

We rely on the monthly committed bucket for predictable costs — this overage would push us past our commit and into a large charge. Please advise next steps; we can share a short internal timeline if that helps.

Best,
Samira
Head of Platform
Fjord Analytics

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexplained spike on June 9 — asking to hold invoice

Samira — I reviewed the export and SRE correlation notes. Concretely:

- We see ~2.3M tokens attributable to api_key: stg-FA-x12 during 2027-06-09 02:18–04:44 PDT.
- Approximately 72% of that traffic was routed through the same model shard as your prod key due to shared routing policy during a short surge window.
- Our attribution logic bills per api_key; however, if traffic is proxied through a shared pool and cached kv lookups have cross-key cache hits, billing can surface under the shard rather than the original key in aggregated views. The raw request_id traces still map back to stg-FA-x12 (see cols request_id and api_key in the CSV).

As a one-time, good-faith resolution we propose: a provisional credit equal to 100% of the token overage (billing amount excluding tax) for this incident, pending your confirmation and a short amendment acknowledging staging-to-prod key segregation best practices. We will issue a credit memo and reverse the VAT portion on your next statement once we have a signed amendment. If that sounds acceptable Samira, Ill prepare a provisional credit memo for your records.

I attached a draft credit memo and a short amendment template (signed amendment will be required to finalize accounting).

Attachment: provisional-credit-memo-FA-0611.pdf
—Markus
Finance — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai

Thanks, team — this is helpful and fair. We confirm that the staging key was unintentionally promoted in the Canary pipeline; the attached signed amendment (signed-amendment-FA-v2.pdf) is our acceptance of the segregation guidance and paperwork for the credit.

We accept the provisional credit for the token overage (please ensure VAT reversal appears on our July statement). Quick ask: can you also include the per-request request_id slice in the provisional memo so our auditors can reconcile? Otherwise well close out this incident.

Appreciate the speedy attention.

—Samira
